thread:
olivia: quick ask — can someone run a short nsys + torch.prof capture on rtx-60 for model `redwood-v2-quant`? low-priority but want a quick flamegraph and kv-cache snapshot for a small batch=1 inference. should be ~100 steps. please scrub any creds before upload.

jamal: I can take this. do you want full `--capture-range` or the lightweight sample?

olivia: lightweight sample is fine. want kernel timeline + python ops. include `--nvtx` and torch.prof with record_shapes. 100 steps w/ 10 warmup.

kira: command i usually run: 
```
NSYS_OUTPUT=nsys_minirun.qdrep 
TORCH_PROF_OUT=tp_minirun.json 
python -m scripts.run_infer \  --model redwood-v2-quant \  --batch_size 1 \  --steps 100 \  --warmup_steps 10 \  --use_kv_cache True \  --capture_nsys $NSYS_OUTPUT \  --torchprof_out $TORCH_PROF_OUT
```
attach `--device cuda:0` if you want explicit mapping.

sean: small note — set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` only if you're debugging, it slows kernels. not needed for perf traces.

jamal: thanks. after run i'll scrub logs for IPs/ARNs and upload. preferred upload path?

olivia: put them in s3://redwood-profiling/eng-runtime/olivia/mini-nsys/ with directory `$(date +%Y%m%d)-<short-desc>` and drop a link here. label kv-cache state `kv_seq=1` or `kv_seq=full` depending on warmup.

artifact-bot: reminder: uploads >100MB should use multipart uploader. use `artifact-uploader --bucket redwood-profiling --acl internal <files>` — it will return a presigned link.

jamal: ran it, attached minimal flamegraph and qdrep. scrubbed. link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-profiling/eng-runtime/olivia/20240223-mini-nsys/nsys_minirun.qdrep (public=false)

kira: quick glance — i see heavy attention kernels at step ~13, kv miss around step 8. can you also capture a small torchprof snippet with `record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True`?

jamal: re-run queued, will do 30-step focused capture around the hot region (steps 8-20). will include `--torchprof-focus start=8 end=20`.

olivia: awesome. when you upload second artifact, ping `@eng-runtime` and add the small flame SVG. also add brief notes: gpu model, driver (nvidia 535), cuda, pytorch hash. makes triage faster.

jamal: noted. ETA ~30m. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

infra-ops: FYI if you need a reserved rtx-60 slot, ping this thread and i'll bump the job to priority queue for 1 hour.

sean: small suggestion for triage doc — add a 1-liner: "what changed since last good run" (model weights, quantization, or batch pattern). saves us a lot of churn.

olivia: agreed. i'll paste quick diff if any. thanks team.
